This study surveyed 29 clinical trials of microbiome modulators in colorectal cancer (CRC) as of June 30, 2025, finding that the pipeline is predominantly early-phase (Phase I, I/II, and II), with no mention of completed Phase 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) publishing primary endpoints like overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS). It reports efficacy data from Phase II trials (e.g., RENMIN-215 trial showing 20% ORR and 9.6 months mPFS with FMT plus ICIs in MSS CRC) and meta-analyses of early-phase trials, explicitly stating that 'the clinical pipeline for MMs in CRC remains predominantly early-phase'. This confirms the absence of completed large-scale Phase 3 evidence in the surveyed literature.

This study describes an investigator-initiated, randomized, phase II trial (NCT06030037) evaluating P+L versus P+L plus responder-derived fecal microbiota transplantation (R-FMT) in PD-1 resistant/refractory melanoma. The text specifies the intervention protocol: R-FMT is derived from donors with durable response (mPFS ≥24 months) following prior PD-1 ICI, screened for infectious agents, and administered via endoscopy on D1 and D42 followed by oral capsules. The primary endpoint is objective response rate (ORR) by Blinded Independent Central Review, with secondary endpoints including progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Translational endpoints include immune activation, metagenomic engraftment, and transcriptomic analyses. Enrollment has commenced, but no efficacy results are reported.
